title: Fair or unfair? cases
subject: Islamic Studies
unit: Summer 1: Dealings with others and Important Lessons
source: Seeded from islamic-studies/y9 lesson 32 (Pupil PDF worksheet: fair or unfair? cases)
intro: Lesson 32: Fairness in business: weights, contracts and wages. To understand how Islam protects fairness in weights and measures, written contracts and paying workers

questions.q: Explain how Islam protects fairness in business. (4 marks, our own question)
questions.a: It forbids short measure (83:1-3); commands written contracts for debts (2:282); requires workers to be paid their full wage (Bukhari).
questions.model: Point 1: fair measures. Develop: 'Woe to those who give less' (83:1). Point 2: workers' rights. Develop: Allah opposes the one who does not pay a worker (Bukhari).

questions.q: Fair or unfair? In the portal response box, judge three cases: a shop's scales set 50g light; a boss who pays a month late without reason; a friend who lends £200 with no written note. For each: the principle, the evidence and the fix. Start: 'Case 1 is unfair because ...'
questions.a: Short measure (83:1-3), fix the scales; late wages (Bukhari hadith qudsi), pay on time; write the loan (2:282)
questions.model: Teacher does case 1: 'Unfair: it is tatfif, condemned in 83:1-3. Fix: recalibrate the scales and refund customers.'

questions.q: what modern laws in the UK protect the same things?
questions.a: Trading standards on weights, contract law, the national minimum wage

questions.q: The longest ayah in the Qur'an (2:282) is about ...
Back to our ponder: why warn about weights so strongly?
questions.a: Small cheating harms many and shows no fear of the Day
